canIDoThis.heading: Can I do this?
canIDoThis.subhead: Three quick questions. Spoiler: the answer is yes.

questions.question: I've never written code.
questions.answer: Perfect. Most of last year's best products came from people who prompted well, not people who coded. The boot camp teaches the tools from zero.

questions.question: I don't have a team.
questions.answer: No problem. Apply solo and we place you on a balanced team of two to four, mixing experienced and new builders.

questions.question: I can be there all day on Friday, Feb 5.
questions.answer: Great, that's the one hard requirement. The boot camp is where everyone gets their tools, their team and their starting point.
questions.answerIfNo: Full attendance on Feb 5 is the one hard requirement, so check your calendar before you apply. You can answer "Maybe" on the form, but confirmed applicants get priority.

result.heading: You're in the right place.
result.body: That's everything the hackathon needs from you. The rest we teach.

whatIsIt.heading: What is a hackathon?
body: A hackathon is a short, focused build sprint. Teams get a real problem from a real company and have about a week to turn it into a working product using AI tools.
Nothing to do with security or breaking into systems. Think of it as a case competition where the deliverable is a product people can click on, not a slide deck.
No coding experience needed. No team needed. The boot camp gets everyone to the same starting line.

whoCanApply.heading: Who can apply
whoCanApply.lead: Every McCombs MBA student. Experience optional.

groups.title: Full-time MBA
groups.body: First-year and second-year full-time MBA students get priority for seats.

groups.title: Part-time and TEMBA
groups.body: Working professionals are welcome. Feb 5 is a Friday and full-day attendance is required, so check your calendar first.

notes: No build or coding experience required. Veterans, career switchers and first-time builders are exactly who this is for.
Apply with a team of two to four, or solo and we'll place you.
One application per person, even if you're applying as a team.

journey.heading: How it works
journey.subhead: Four stages, one week, one working product.

steps.title: Boot camp
steps.body: A full day on campus. Learn the AI tools, see what's possible, meet the partner companies and their problems. Everyone leaves with the same toolkit.

steps.title: Team up
steps.body: Teams of two to four lock in. Solo applicants are placed on balanced teams. Each team picks a company problem to solve.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: A week to turn the problem into a working product. Mentors and office hours along the way. Work from anywhere.

steps.title: Demo day
steps.body: Show what you built to the partner companies, McCombs leadership and the Austin tech community. Winners announced.

selection.heading: How selection works
selection.lead: About 100 seats. Here's how we fill them.
points: Full attendance at the Feb 5 boot camp is required. Applicants who can't make it won't be selected.
Teams are preferred. If you already have two to four people, apply together using the same team name.
Full-time MBA applicants get priority, then part-time and TEMBA, then solo applicants.
If applications exceed seats, we'll publish the exact cut rule before decisions go out.
Decisions by email by TODO Dec 11, 2026.
selection.closeNote: Applications close Friday, Dec 4, 2026 at 11:59 PM CT.

items.q: How much time does it take?
items.a: One full day on Friday, Feb 5 for the boot camp, then about a week of building on your own schedule with your team. Most teams spend 15 to 25 hours over the build week. Demo day is a few hours.

items.q: Do I need to know how to code?
items.a: No. The boot camp teaches the AI tools from scratch, and the tools do the heavy lifting. If you can describe a problem clearly, you can build.

items.q: Which AI tools do we use, and who pays?
items.a: TODO We're confirming tool access and credits with partners. You'll have what you need to build without paying out of pocket. Details on this page before applications close.

items.q: What if I don't have a team?
items.a: Apply solo. We place solo applicants on teams of two to four, balancing experience so every team has a mix of builders and first-timers.

items.q: How big can a team be?
items.a: Two to four people. Everyone on the team submits their own application with the same team name.
A laptop, a charger and a problem you'd love to solve. Everything else is provided.
TODO Announcing soon. Each partner brings a real problem for teams to work on.
Your application is used only for hackathon selection and team placement. It's stored in a sheet shared with the organizing team, and EIDs are deleted 30 days after demo day.

form.title: Apply
form.intro: About three minutes. One question at a time. Your answers save in this browser so you can come back.

name.label: What's your full name?
name.help: As it appears on your UT record.

eid.label: What's your UT EID?
eid.help: Letters followed by numbers, like abc123. We use it to make sure each person has one application.

email.label: What's your UT email?
email.help: Must end in utexas.edu. Decisions go to this address.

program.label: Which program are you in?
program.help: Full-time MBA students get priority. Everyone else is eligible.

feb5.label: Can you attend the full boot camp on Friday, Feb 5, 2027?
feb5.help: It runs all day on campus. Full attendance is required.
feb5.noNote: Full attendance at the boot camp is required for selection. You can still submit, but you won't be selected unless this changes.

week.label: Are you available for the rest of hackathon week?
week.help: TODO Build week dates coming soon. Teams build on their own schedule; plan on 15 to 25 hours.

applyingAs.label: Are you applying with a team or solo?
applyingAs.help: Teams are two to four people. Solo applicants are placed on a team.

teamName.label: What's your team name?
teamName.help: Every teammate enters this same name on their own application. Capitalization doesn't matter.

teammateEmails.label: What are your teammates' UT emails?
teammateEmails.help: One to three addresses, not including yours. Each teammate still submits their own application.

aiSubscription.label: What AI tools do you use today?
aiSubscription.help: Pick the closest match. There's no wrong answer; it helps us balance teams and plan support.

buildExperience.label: Have you built anything with AI or no-code tools before?
buildExperience.help: Honest answers help us place solo applicants on balanced teams.

why.label: Why do you want to do this?
why.help: Up to 300 characters. A couple of sentences is plenty.

consent.label: One last thing
consent.text: I understand my application data is used only for hackathon selection and team placement, is shared only with the organizing team, and is deleted 30 days after demo day.

review.heading: Check your answers

beforeOpen.heading: Applications open Nov 9
beforeOpen.body: Come back on Monday, Nov 9, 2026 to apply. In the meantime, read how it works and round up a team.

afterClose.heading: Applications are closed
afterClose.body: Thanks for the interest. Decisions go out by email by Dec 11, 2026. Questions? Email the organizing team.

confirmation.heading: You're in the running.
confirmation.body: We've got your application. You'll get a confirmation email at {email} in the next few minutes, and a decision by {decisionsBy}.
confirmation.resubmittedBody: We've updated your earlier application. The newest answers are the ones we'll use.
confirmation.teamNote: Remind your teammates to apply with the team name "{teamName}". Every seat needs its own application.

failure.heading: That didn't go through
failure.body: Your answers are still here. Try again, and if it keeps failing, email us and we'll take your application by hand.
